what: Both tenant changes, verified. SCAN_INTAKE is Tenant again; FETCH_ALL refuses the caller it served on 2026-09-22. Each is evidenced by a fresh artefact from the tenant, not by a report that the change was made.

scanIntake.reads: The same flow id the 2026-09-18 tenant read returned as All now exports as Tenant, modified 2026-09-24T04:55:02Z. DECISIONS.md D6 is satisfied again and npm run triggerauth is measuring the deployed posture rather than a superseded export.

fetchAll.howItWasFixed: Not the way this repository proposed, and better. The proposal was to move the real expression INTO Compose_FetchAll_Permitted. What was done instead leaves that Compose at true and compares it against the real expression in the condition itself — equals(true, <check>) — which is the same decision and removes the parked action entirely. The else branch, which previously held no actions at all, now discriminates two cases the proposal collapsed into one: a caller present in the directory but lacking the permission gets 403, and a caller in no directory row at all gets 401.

refusal.message: The caller is not in DGO_UserDirectory, or is not active.

sameInputOppositeOutcome.reads: The identical caller — no identity, matching no directory row — received the estate on 2026-09-22 and a 401 on 2026-09-24. That is the fix demonstrated on the input that exposed it, which is the only demonstration worth having.

whatThisEstablishes: That SCAN_INTAKE's trigger requires tenant authentication again, read from a fresh export of the same flow id.
That FETCH_ALL refuses an unidentified caller in production, with 401 and a named reason, on the same input that previously returned 6.1 MB.
That the parked expression is gone, so there is one decision in that flow rather than two.
whatItExplicitlyDoesNotEstablish: That FETCH_ALL authenticates its caller. Compose_FetchAll_Caller still reads userEmail from the REQUEST BODY, so a caller who names an active directory user is authorised as that user. The refusal proved here is of a caller who named NOBODY. That is G-04, it is unchanged, and it is now the whole of the problem rather than part of it.
That the other endpoints refuse anything. This is one flow. The audit finds no other decision pinned to a constant, but that is a statement about one defect shape, not a clean bill.
That the 2026-09-22 disclosure is resolved. Fixing the flow does not answer whether that release of directory data is notifiable; that remains the agency's to decide.
